lark_e04_entry.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_entry.text: On Day Twenty-nine, Lin's second accepted shift began with a shared safety orientation led by the gallery keeper. Copying, route recording and dispatch work could each bring a person near the freight passage, so its cleared exits belonged in every role's first week. It was ordinary paid instruction within this shift, not a new powered practice task. Before the keeper arrived, Qin stopped at the receiving point under his own collecting duty. He asked whether she wished to join the household's evening meal after her shift.

lark_e04_entry_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_entry_002.text: They had already discussed the corrected repair account and its actual dispatch payments before Lin accepted her work role on Day Twenty-four. The resulting ease or caution still belonged in their acquaintance; today's meal invitation did not ask her to reinterpret those completed opportunities. Qin kept his current load paper beside the remaining basket request and asked a different ordinary question. Shan Fang would be cooking beans after her own teaching receiving. Lin accepted the invitation, saying she would bring a little salt and arrive only after her shift's actual ending.

lark_e04_walk_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_001.text: The keeper began with the public exit board, not the timber beneath it. A painted upward arrow meant the ordinary market stair; a low square meant the rigger's stone shelter. The third mark identified a branch currently closed pending inspection. Lin read the marks back before following him. The keeper asked why they should not simply use words. A carrier beside him said words were useful until the board turned away from the person carrying a basket. They demonstrated where its face disappeared at the turn.

lark_e04_walk_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_002.text: Lin walked within the cleared line with only her small notebook. Her present clinic note permitted that ordinary activity; it supplied no loaded gallery test. The keeper stopped the first group at a landing large enough for them to wait outside moving freight. He introduced the route's responsible posts and explained which one would receive a changed condition. Lin noticed how easy it would have been to imagine every man near a rope had authority to alter the route. Their actual duties divided the work more carefully than their similar clothes suggested.

lark_e04_walk_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_003.text: The lowest timber rail carried several shallow scratches. A visitor called them evidence of a recent dangerous strike. The keeper showed the public maintenance record identifying ordinary basket contact at that inspected position and its last qualified check. A new scratch could still need examination. The old marks did not become harmless merely because they were familiar, and they did not become a collapse because a newcomer disliked their appearance. Lin waited while the keeper compared the current condition with its actual reference.

lark_e04_walk_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_004.text: At the turn beyond it, the path widened enough that an ordinary carrier could rest without entering the load line. The rigger's stone shelter stood below a roof that did not rely on the suspended gallery. Lin asked where its limit was recorded. The keeper pointed to its accepted occupancy and use notice, which excluded new load storage. An exit could remain available for people without becoming an overflow warehouse. The carrier said the last supplier had tried to put baskets there during a wet afternoon.

lark_e04_walk_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_005.text: The keeper explained how the posted guide would halt new entry before directing people toward that shelter. The guide would not drag a load through its door to prove he had evacuated successfully. Qualified crew could isolate and remove freight under their own procedure afterward. Lin pictured an emergency in which every useful-looking object became something she ought to catch. She returned to the actual sequence on the board. Clear roles would matter most when a frightened person wanted to do several of them at once.

lark_e04_walk_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_006.text: Jiang Tao met the orientation at the cleared upper station. The bell relay remained disconnected while he checked its ordinary controls with his accepted inspection team. He showed Lin the separate fuel custody label before pointing out where a rated command input would sit. Association-owned reserve stones powered the sound circuit. A novice's half-unit input limit did not become the bell's energy source, and her hand would not carry its timber load. Today she would observe the qualified check without adding personal qi.

lark_e04_walk_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_007.text: The station's ordinary bell rope passed through a guide above the viewing rail. A rigger moved it while another worker watched the sound mechanism from its actual safe post. Lin saw the rope respond before she heard the bell below. Jiang asked the positions to be recorded and repeated the check from a closer cleared listening place. The apparent delay changed with the listening position. That result supported an ordinary distance question and separated it from a control delay that would need its own measured test.

lark_e04_walk_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_008.text: Lin found the explanation disappointing for a moment. She had arrived with the image of a wrong bell warning before a broken gallery. A competent survey could give her an answer less dramatic than the pattern she wanted. Jiang asked whether she would record the changed listening place or only the first alarming observation. She wrote both. The gallery still had actual maintenance questions. Those questions did not become clearer by adding a sound fault the comparison had not supported.

lark_e04_walk_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_009.text: One inspection worker found moisture on the removable reference cover and stopped before lifting it over the isolated contacts. The supervisor received the changed condition and directed ordinary drying and recheck. Lin stayed outside the working area. Her new job did not make a pair of unasked helping hands useful in a station whose safe handling roles had been agreed already. She watched the worker set the cover on a dry supported board and admired how little ceremony a properly received stop required.

lark_e04_walk_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_010.text: After the station, the keeper led the group along the public viewing path toward the upper scree. The actual freight branch there remained closed. A carrier pointed to tracks beneath the stone lip and said the cloudhound had been back. Lin had seen a territorial scree hunter elsewhere, but this report concerned an animal here. She could recognize a species description without importing another individual's history or behavior. The keeper asked everyone to stay at the posted viewing line while he checked with the current upper-route observer.

lark_e04_walk_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_011.text: A cloudhound appeared above the scree before the observer returned. Its body moved low along the pale rock, then stopped near a broken shrub where a smaller movement disappeared into a crevice. Lin stayed behind the line. The creature looked toward the group and changed its stance; no spoken permission or prophecy accompanied it. The keeper directed the viewers back to the larger landing without trying to prove a human right by frightening the animal from its ordinary ground.

lark_e04_walk_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_012.text: They waited until the current observer confirmed its position and the existing closure. The animal's appearance did not establish who had broken a support, when a worker had crossed the branch or what caused a past freight delay. It did establish a present reason to keep visitors from treating the upper scree as an attractive shortcut. Lin recorded only the observed movement and the keeper's actual instruction. The closed branch would stay closed while its qualified route and habitat questions were received through their proper posts.

lark_e04_walk_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_013.text: The carrier who had named the hound said his brother once sold a story in which one rescued a falling cultivator. He wanted to know whether Lin believed it. She said she had not witnessed that rescue. He said the story sold better whenever the cultivator was described as important. Jiang, returning from his station, asked whether the brother had ever sold a version with a tired ordinary carrier. The carrier said the audience usually asked why such a person had been standing somewhere dangerous in the first place.

lark_e04_walk_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_walk_014.text: Lin laughed, then thought about how easily her own stage could make an observer's mistake seem like an event the mountain had designed for her. The cloudhound continued hunting beyond the line. It did not need to be her guardian or the keeper of a secret to alter what people could safely do around it. The keeper showed the group the approved lower alternative before the orientation ended. It was less beautiful, a little longer, and connected to a stone landing whose condition had actually been checked.

lark_e04_role_gate.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_role_gate.text: The keeper received the shared orientation as part of Lin's second ordinary shift. Her selected primary assignment determined the remaining work within those same six hours. Copying, route records and dispatch comparison would use the observed exits differently. She went to the actual role she had accepted rather than assuming a useful walk had made her available for every waiting task.

lark_e04_copy_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_copy_001.text: In the copying room, Shan gave Lin the public exit board's authorized source and asked for a trial notice readers could use from the market stair. Lin drew the three marks first, then discovered her arrows depended on the viewer facing the same way as the person who had painted the original. Shan turned the sheet around. Lin felt the route she had just walked become difficult to explain. She wrote the receiving point beside the direction and asked the actual keeper to verify the offered wording.

lark_e04_copy_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_copy_002.text: The household reader who tried the first copy could read its large closure heading but not distinguish the low shelter mark from a basket-store square. Lin darkened the shape and kept the shelter's no-storage condition next to it. The reader said she had wanted to collect a parcel, not take an examination in signs. Shan asked which one fact she would look for first. She wanted the place she should go if the original desk closed. Their next copy began there instead of with the association's impressive name.

lark_e04_copy_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_copy_003.text: A school pupil offered to color the cloudhound into the notice as a warning. Lin told him the present upper closure required the actual keeper's words rather than a picture implying the animal alone had caused it. He made the hound red anyway on his own private drawing. Shan let him keep it out of the public source folder and asked what the animal might have been doing before the viewers arrived. He said hunting something that probably did not know it was in a lesson. Lin liked that answer enough to laugh.

lark_e04_copy_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_copy_004.text: The keeper accepted one revised public notice after comparing it with the current clearance. Its dated shelter and receiving point could now be read from the stair's ordinary standing place. A second proposed picture remained the pupil's own, outside the official copying. Lin's selected desk work had turned the shared orientation into a usable public page. She had not walked every future reader's route, and the keeper retained the actual right to change the notice when conditions changed. Shan received the rest of her six-hour shift before the ending bell.

lark_e04_copy_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_copy_005.text: When Qin next passed the stair, he stopped to read the new large receiving line. He said it would keep his mother from asking his daughter to explain the symbols each time a load delayed the desk. Lin asked him to tell the actual keeper if the wording failed her at a real closure. Qin said he would, and told her the hound in the child's drawing looked more like an angry turnip. She had chosen a job that could make a familiar household's next question easier, and still leave its people free to mock the art.

lark_e04_route_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_route_001.text: The route keeper took Lin back to the ordinary standing points recorded during the orientation. Her remaining shift compared what different users could see, without carrying freight or entering the closed upper branch. A short household reader could read the public board only when a waiting carrier moved aside. Lin recorded the occupied view, then asked the keeper where readers were actually expected to wait. The marked space belonged to the load queue. Two accepted uses had been placed where they obstructed each other.

lark_e04_route_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_route_002.text: The keeper called the current public receiving attendant and the queue supervisor to compare the conflict at its actual place. Lin did not make one group vanish from her drawing to improve the other group's route. The supervisor moved the next ordinary waiting position within his existing clearance; the attendant received the change and tested the view with the household reader. The board became visible without widening timber or shifting a load station. The carrier whose waiting place changed asked whether his next basket would still reach the guide without an extra turn.

lark_e04_route_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_route_003.text: They repeated his unloaded approach under the keeper's supervision. The new waiting position added an ordinary turn and retained the cleared movement. Lin put that extra action beside the improved reading view. The carrier complained that a person drawing routes could always improve them by borrowing someone else's steps. The household reader thanked him for moving. He looked embarrassed and said he was still allowed to complain. Lin recorded the practical result without selecting which expression would make the association's adjustment look most cheerful.

lark_e04_route_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_route_004.text: The keeper received the dated route comparison and its actual revised waiting point. It would need another check if a new load arrangement changed the view again. Lin's second shift ended with a concrete movement improvement and a carrier bearing a small added turn. She had performed the ordinary accepted role, not certified the supports or entered the hound's scree. Four copper became due after the whole received shift. She could feel the work becoming familiar in a way that made its inconveniences more particular rather than less important.

lark_e04_route_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_route_005.text: Qin looked at the new waiting line during his next collection. He agreed the public board was easier to see, then asked whether the carrier's complaint had been kept with the change. Lin showed him the dated note. He nodded and said his own daughter's drawings improved the kitchen by moving every adult out of the way. The remark made her laugh and reminded her how much route work depended on people who would remain present after the diagram had been finished. She had chosen to keep meeting those people at the place their steps crossed.

lark_e04_dispatch_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_dispatch_001.text: At the wage desk, the reader asked Lin to compare how an actual closure would change today's accepted dispatch scopes. The terms distinguished halted entry, canceled departure and completed delivery; the public exit board did not tell a carrier what each change paid. Lin read the specific waiting and cancellation clauses before preparing a trial explanation. She could remember He Xi's ordinary two or four copper without importing those earlier prices into contracts held by people here.

lark_e04_dispatch_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_dispatch_002.text: A carrier with a booked upper-store load wanted to know whether reaching the rigger's shelter would count as delivery if the gallery closed. Lin showed him the actual named receiving point. The shelter was an exit for people, not the store buying his cargo movement. Its safe use would not complete the delivered scope. The reader asked what paid waiting would follow the particular closure. They compared the offered condition and put the relevant receiving contact beside it so the carrier could ask a real question when the event occurred.

lark_e04_dispatch_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_dispatch_003.text: The apprentice prepared a new public scope note and wanted the association's seal printed larger than the cancellation line. Lin asked which part the carrier would need when his load stopped. He moved the cancellation line up. The seal still identified the source, while the ordinary words did the harder work of describing what had been bought. A household reader then asked whether the note applied to her parcel collection. The wage reader directed her to its different accepted terms instead of making a clear note universal by placing it on a public board.

lark_e04_dispatch_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_dispatch_004.text: The responsible wage keeper received the completed scope explanation and retained its specific contract reference. Lin's second ordinary shift ended at the listed bell, making another four-copper wage due after receiving. Her work had made a future interruption easier to compare with paid duties. It had not prevented a closure, created a storage place in the shelter or restored a missed load. She had chosen a desk where the consequences of a sound exit could arrive as an unhappy but accurate amount at the bottom of somebody's slip.

lark_e04_dispatch_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_dispatch_005.text: Qin read the new scope note before his next scheduled turn. He asked the wage reader to confirm its condition against his actual load terms instead of accepting Lin's familiarity as a guarantee. She was glad he did and more hurt by the distance than she had expected. Both feelings could fit beneath one ordinary job. Qin took the confirmed line back to his dispatcher. Lin had chosen to help people make scope questions precise, which meant learning not to confuse being personally trusted with being entitled to replace their actual source.

lark_e04_evening_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_001.text: The receiving keeper signed Lin's second shift at its sixth hour. Four copper became due for work completed, and Qin carried the pay envelope down with his own freight papers. Eight earned copper now sat apart from Lin's remaining road money. She paid one copper for a pear at the lower stall, cut it with the seller's knife, and shared the larger half with the child who had drawn a cloudhound shaped like a turnip.

lark_e04_evening_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_002.text: Jiang Tao waited until she had eaten before opening the apparatus room. The visit lay outside her paid shift and could be declined. Lin went because the naked comparison strip interested her more than the polished cover. It rested between two ordinary screw clamps, neither bearing her qi nor the pressure of a suspended load. Jiang showed where a cracked support would be visible, then invited her to look from the opposite side. The same scratch disappeared behind a screw head. A good inspection, he said, needed more than a confident first position.

lark_e04_evening_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_003.text: He offered no test of her channels that evening. Instead, he asked her to make a drawing somebody else could use. Lin marked the scratch by its place on the metal and omitted the movable screw head as a fixed reference. Jiang moved the head again and found her mark. He put it beside a previous drawing that had failed for exactly the reason hers now avoided. Lin preferred that comparison to being told she had an unusual eye.

lark_e04_evening_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_004.text: The room's lantern hissed when the wick found an uneven pocket of oil. Jiang trimmed it with the scissors hanging by the door. Lin had mistaken a similar hiss for a hot comparison strip during an earlier observation. Tonight she watched the cause and felt the uncomfortable pleasure of losing a plausible explanation. Jiang wrote the time of the trim in his own operating notes. Her sketch stayed in the practice folder.

lark_e04_evening_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_005.text: Outside, Qin's daughter had tied her turnip hound to a stick and was chasing real chickens with it. Shan Fang called her away from the market's loose gravel. The child objected that a cloudhound would not obey its mother. Qin replied that a cloudhound could purchase its own supper, whereas this one had already eaten his pear. The child lowered the paper animal, considered the price of supper, and came indoors on terms she described as temporary.

lark_e04_evening_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_006.text: The family ate beans thickened with crushed millet. Lin brought a little salt as an invited contribution, bought for one of her own earned copper. Qin tasted it before putting it into the pot. He had once let a guest improve a meal with something intended for cleaning a copper vessel. Shan Fang said the story grew less believable each winter. Qin answered that its usefulness grew with the winter visitors. His daughter wanted to know whether the guest had survived. They told her the guest had returned for three more meals and learned to ask.

lark_e04_evening_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_007.text: Lin did not need to recount the whole day's work at the table. Shan Fang already knew her own teaching hours and wanted to talk about the empty room below the shrine. Several families hoped to use it for winter mending. The shrine keeper wanted somebody to remove the fallen plaster first, and the families disagreed about whether that counted as a gift or work owed by the keeper. Qin had offered his cart on a clear morning. Nobody had accepted a date. The argument had reached the cheerful stage where every proposed morning suited nobody.

lark_e04_evening_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_008.text: The empty room had once belonged to a woman who sold woven caps. Her nephew still kept two boxes there, although he lived across the river. Shan Fang would not agree to move them on the strength of a rumor that he no longer wanted them. This irritated one of her neighbors. Lin suggested asking for a reply that named the boxes separately from the room. Shan Fang said she would put that question in tomorrow's ordinary letter.

lark_e04_evening_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_009.text: The child fell asleep against Qin's knee while the adults were still discussing plaster. He tried to stand without waking her and failed twice. On the third attempt she woke, declared herself entirely awake, and leaned against Lin instead. Lin could not take her weight safely on the recovering shoulder. She shifted her stool and let the child rest against its back. Shan Fang saw the change and placed a folded cloth there. Lin stayed long enough for the kettle to boil again.

lark_e04_evening_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_010.text: Walking back to her lodging, she heard somebody playing the narrow flute used at freight departures. The player kept dropping the same note. Behind a closed shutter, another voice supplied it with ruthless accuracy. The player began again and dropped a different note. Lin stood under the eave until the tune finally reached its ending. Then both unseen musicians argued about which mistakes had been deliberate. A successful mountain night could contain that sort of dispute: no falling stone, no examination, only people unwilling to surrender the last word.

lark_e04_evening_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_011.text: On Day Thirty, there was no paid shift on Lin's accepted schedule. She washed her undershirt in cold water and hung it where passing smoke would not blacken it. Her shoulder tired with the wringing, so she pressed the cloth against the basin's clean side instead. The slower method occupied more of the morning. It left her arm available for the ordinary strength exercise the clinician had assigned. She counted the movements rather than the discomfort, stopped at the agreed limit, and went downstairs while the cloth still dripped.

lark_e04_evening_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_012.text: Qin was repairing a wheel with a neighbor whose patience exceeded his speech. Lin watched them remove the axle without offering a strength she did not have. Qin wanted the wheel straight quickly. The neighbor wanted to find why it had rubbed. A misplaced washer appeared after the second bearing was opened. Its edges had polished themselves into an attractive circle. Qin held it like a coin he had accidentally earned. The neighbor laid it on the windowsill and refused to let him celebrate until the wheel turned freely.

lark_e04_evening_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_013.text: The repair consumed the morning, so Qin could not lend his cart for an unaccepted plaster clearing that day. Nobody had organized a crew around the absent promise. Shan Fang sent her letter about the stored boxes and used her own free hour to sew a tear in a winter sleeve. When work began, it would need an actual meeting.

lark_e04_evening_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_014.text: That afternoon, Chen Rui came up the stairs carrying a packet sealed in plain paper. He had supplier business at the upper market and had asked the lodging keeper whether Lin would receive a visitor. The keeper asked Lin before directing him to her door. He did not come in until she invited him. The packet contained a drawing of a freight signal joint, not a present. His client wanted an informed comparison against the association's existing method. Chen asked whether she would hear the request before deciding what access she could offer.

lark_e04_evening_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_015.text: Lin listened in the common room. Chen's client could explain its own joint and show a sample under its own terms. It could not use her employment as permission to inspect the association's closed appendix. Lin had not yet been given that appendix herself. Chen nodded, somewhat relieved that she had stated the awkward part before he reached it. He had been paid to bring a request, not to bring back a secret. They agreed to ask the actual keeper together on Day Thirty Five, after Lin's next accepted shifts.

lark_e04_evening_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_016.text: Chen stayed for tea that he bought from the lodging keeper. He asked whether the lower road still smelled of wet wool. Lin said it smelled of onions now, which was not an improvement the merchants had sought. He had travelled that road years earlier with a chest that contained every sample his employer owned. He remembered every stone as an enemy. Lin wondered whether any of them had recognized him on his return. He said the stones were professionally discreet. She found herself glad of the visit before remembering its business.

lark_e04_evening_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_017.text: He left before the lamp was needed. Lin did not escort him beyond the lodging stair, where the shoulder's dull tiredness had become a sharper request for rest. She watched him stop to ask a vendor about a broken buckle and understood how much of his travel consisted of small repairs that no account of his negotiations would mention. That evening she wrote down the proposed meeting date. The page had enough room below it for an invitation to Qin's household if they wished to attend.

lark_e04_evening_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_018.text: Her next accepted shift fell on Day Thirty One. The receiving keeper assigned the same ordinary role she had agreed to perform, within its posted limits, and checked the completed work at the end. The day's weather was fine enough that people complained about the previous day's cold with an air of personal victory. Lin ate her noon meal on the stair beside a porter who was trying to learn his daughter's multiplication song. He could carry a load through three landings without stumbling and could not get beyond seven times four.

lark_e04_evening_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_019.text: She knew the song and helped with its troublesome line while they waited for the receiving bell. The porter explained that his daughter refused to accept the right answer unless it came with the tune. When the bell sounded, he left for his assigned loading place. She returned to her own task. At evening receiving, another four copper was paid for the completed six hours. Her cumulative accepted work now amounted to eighteen hours and twelve copper, with the next shift still ahead of her.

lark_e04_evening_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_020.text: Day Thirty Two brought the reply concerning the shrine room. The nephew wanted his cap molds retained but permitted the old broken reed boxes to be discarded after the keeper checked them for remaining tools. He could not come before the late month. Shan Fang read the reply to the families gathered at the room's doorway. A woman who had argued for clearing everything immediately picked up the first box and found three usable needles in its corner. She handed them to the keeper without concealing her earlier opinion. The room became less hypothetical.

lark_e04_evening_021.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_021.text: Lin joined for an hour of light sweeping after the keeper accepted the families' actual morning plan. She stayed below the shoulder's comfortable height and left the heavy plaster to two people who had agreed to lift it. Qin's cart received the sacks at its rated weight. The neighbor who had repaired the wheel checked the axle after the first trip and pronounced it dull enough to trust. Shan Fang put the cap molds in a dry corner, then washed the little window from its sill.

lark_e04_evening_022.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_022.text: The new room smelled of dust, soap, and damp stone. One of the women set out stools as if winter had already begun. Another wanted a shelf before anybody used it. They moved the stools aside to measure the proposed shelf, then moved them back for tea. Lin drank from a chipped cup and listened to the women discuss whose nephew could plane a straight board. The permission to clear a room had not made them agree about furnishing it. It had given their disagreement a clean floor on which to stand.

lark_e04_evening_023.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_023.text: Qin carried the discarded plaster down to the permitted rubble place, where the workers separated reusable stone from fine dust. It was slower than tipping the cart into the ravine. The distinction mattered to the households below, which had water channels along that slope. His daughter walked beside the empty cart on the return and made its shadow into a cloudhound with her stick. Lin was too tired to go with them. She sat at the new room's doorway until the animal's paper head disappeared around the stair.

lark_e04_evening_024.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_024.text: The accepted shift on Day Thirty Four began after two quieter days. Lin found the same shoulder still capable of its work, without claiming that the passage of days had healed it. The keeper received her task at the sixth hour. Four more copper brought the sum paid for four completed shifts to sixteen. A second weekly lodging and meal provision was received under the agreed five copper allocation. Twenty two weeks remained in that part of the appropriation.

lark_e04_evening_025.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_025.text: That evening, the shrine keeper lit the first lamp in the mending room. There were no completed shelves, so the women placed their baskets beneath their stools. Shan Fang brought the torn winter sleeve. Qin came to carry the lamp oil, then stayed to have a button replaced. Lin brought nothing to mend and was told this was an efficient way to enjoy conversation. She sat by the window while a needle passed in and out of cloth. The bell beyond the market sounded once, and every hand continued its small useful movement.

lark_e04_evening_026.speaker: narrator
lark_e04_evening_026.text: The next morning's appointment with the appendix keeper lay ahead of her. Lin had four ordinary shifts behind her, a place at two household tables when invited, and a clearer account of which mountain doors were public. She could arrive at the proper door with a question. The keeper could answer, refuse, or propose different terms. Lin put her completed work papers away and slept before the market opened.
